It was the case of the eviction petitioner - landlord that she had rented out the premises bearing Shop No. 15, in property no. 4415, Gali Bahuji, Pahari Dheeraj, Delhi-110006 to one Sh. Ramesh Kumar on 06.01.1987. However, the said tenant Sh. Ramesh Kumar had parted with possession and sub-let and assigned the same initially to one Sh. Ghanshyam Dass and subsequently to Sh. Bhagwan Dass, who were his father and brother respectively.

It was pleaded by the respondent that he is occupying the demised shop as a tenant and additionally conducting his business from shop no. 5765, Sikli Gran, Factory Road, Nabi Karim, New Delhi-110055.
IK-188721101:L74:restored-v2.stage_note: Parent may contain both party statements and prior findings. Preserve explicit attribution within text, not one uniform truth status.

IK-188721101:L80:restored-v2.text: 3. Petitioner in support of her case examined her attorney, Sh. M.L. Jain as PW-1, who supported the petition. Petitioner also examined two other witnesses, who were shopkeepers having their shops in the vicinity. Both the witnesses deposed that Sh. Bhagwan Dass was running the shop and not respondent Sh. Ramesh Kumar.
IK-188721101:L80:restored-v2.stage_note: Parent may contain both party statements and prior findings. Preserve explicit attribution within text, not one uniform truth status.

IK-188721101:L81:restored-v2.text: 4. Respondent in support of his case examined himself as RW-1 and his brother Sh. Bhagwan Dass, the alleged sub-lessee, as RW-2. Both the witnesses deposed that Sh. Bhagwan Dass was working as an employee and drawing a salary of Rs. 10,000/- per month. The fact of Sh. Bhagwan Dass operating the shop and being in possession of key thereof was admitted. No proof of any other employee was produced. Salary vouchers of payment of salary to Sh. Bhagwan Dass were also not proved.
IK-188721101:L81:restored-v2.stage_note: Parent may contain both party statements and prior findings. Preserve explicit attribution within text, not one uniform truth status.

IK-188721101:L83:restored-v2.text: 5. Trial Court by the impugned judgment took the view that the fact of sub tenancy was not established. Trial court held that it was only a privilege or a licence by the tenant in favour of his brother to use the premises, which licence or privilege could be terminated at the sweet will and pleasure of respondent. Therefore, the arrangement did not amount to assignment or parting with the possession.
IK-188721101:L83:restored-v2.stage_note: Parent may contain both party statements and prior findings. Preserve explicit attribution within text, not one uniform truth status.
